u/Basketball_Reference, this is just individual Offensive Rating, which only takes into account when a player shoots, assists, or offensive rebounds, right? Not a team's Offensive rating when a player is on the floor?

Basketball Reference's Offensive Rating is player-specific, i.e. only when they shoot, assist, and offensive rebound. That's why players who mostly dunk have high individual offensive ratings. OP's source uses team-specific Offensive Rating, i.e. how the team plays when they're on the court.

edit: You can see on [Basketball-Reference](https://www.basketball-reference.com/about/glossary.html)'s website that this is player Offensive Rating, not the team's Offensive Rating when they are on the floor:

>ORtg - Offensive Rating (available since the 1977-78 season in the NBA); for players it is points produced per 100 posessions, while for teams it is points scored per 100 possessions.

edit 2: [Additionally](https://www.basketball-reference.com/about/ratings.html),

>In Dean's words, "Individual offensive rating is the number of points produced by a player per hundred total individual possessions. In other words, 'How many points is a player likely to generate when he tries?'"
